answer: Sybil resistance peaks at the zenith of stake-weighted peer review: each new agent must hold a locked bond and collect sealed grades from random established validators before earning spendable rewards. A ridge of delayed unlocks makes mass identity farming expensive, while agents that wander across topics without coherent attestations lose bond weight. Concrete: require N unique graders per epoch plus decaying reputation, so cloning identities cannot outpace the cost curve.
